basis.enthalpy_reference: JANAF formation enthalpies, used for the duty only

mass_flow.anchor: FOSSEE DWSIM manual Exp 4: 20 kmol/h of stoichiometric CO and H2O (10 each) converted with the stated molar masses

reaction.name: water-gas-shift
reaction.anchor: FOSSEE DWSIM manual Exp 4: CO(g) + H2O(g) <-> CO2(g) + H2(g), base compound carbon monoxide, basis changed to partial pressure and phase to vapour; equilibrium constant from the server's Gibbs energies of formation (no expression given)

reported.name: outlet_mass
reported.anchor: FOSSEE DWSIM manual Exp 4: outlet mass equals the feed mass

reported.name: vapor_monoxide_mass_fraction
reported.anchor: FOSSEE DWSIM manual Exp 4: equilibrium composition: independent: NIST-JANAF tables (janaf.nist.gov) for CO, H2O and CO2 at 800 K: log Kf and fH, K = 10^(logKf(CO2) - logKf(CO) - logKf(H2O)); ideal gas, equal moles so pressure does not matter; computed 2026-11-21 (K = 4.2267, CO conversion 0.6728)

reported.name: outlet_T
reported.anchor: FOSSEE DWSIM manual Exp 4: isothermal reactor at the inlet temperature

reported.name: reactor_duty
reported.anchor: FOSSEE DWSIM manual Exp 4: isothermal duty = extent x heat of reaction at the reactor temperature (a physical expectation, not in the manual); independent: JANAF fH sums, -36.840 kJ/mol at 800 K x 6.728 kmol/h

tolerance.note: 2 percent on compositions and 3 percent on the duty, fixed before the run: JANAF logKf is tabulated to three decimals (about 0.4 percent in K) and DWSIM's constant comes from its own Gibbs-energy database

scenarios.why: the same reactor at 2 bar: the reaction has equal moles on both sides, so an ideal-gas equilibrium composition does not depend on pressure (a check on the equilibrium basis, not in the manual)
the manual's self-learning question 1: equilibrium conversion at 1000 K and 2 bar; K from the same JANAF tables

review.method: K and heats of formation from NIST-JANAF tables; exact stoichiometric balance
